newsitem.title: POLAND: Polifarb Wroclaw to restart work on Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: Polifarb Wroclaw to restart work on Aug 1.

text.p: Polish paintmaker Polifarb Wroclaw, flooded earlier this month, plans to resume full production on August 1, its president said on Tuesday.

"The situation is changing every day, electricity supply is gradually restored....We plan to solve all major problems by the end of July. On August 1 normal production should be resumed," Edward Platek told Reuters.
Platek added that after the plant was flooded its output had shrunk substantially but gradually expanded later.
He said damage appraisal had taken longer than expected but would be completed by Thursday.
Trade in Polifarb Wroclaw has been suspended since July 11 when floodwaters inundated the factory and it will be resumed after the company reports the size of the flood-related damage.
Platek added the company's merger with Polifarb Cieszyn, planned at the end of September, would not be delayed despite the flooding.
"I think there are no obstacles to implementing the programme of the merger between both companies, which is well on its way," Platek said.
Due to the merger Polifarb Cieszyn's shareholders will obtain 53.5 percent of the shares in the merged firm.
The merger was approved by shareholders of both firms in late March.
